President Trump was inaudible during a press conference Monday after the TV pool suspended coverage, with White House-provided video carrying no usable audio of his remarks. Why it matters: It's a remarkable and immediate ramification of Trump's attempt to limit pool access. The pool serves hundreds of journalists, so losing independent TV coverage can limit what the media — and the public — can see and hear. Driving the news: President Trump announced a ban on CNN, MS NOW, and Politico on Friday, confiscating their credentials on Saturday over what he termed "FAKE NEWS". CNN, MS NOW and Politico filed a lawsuit on Monday seeking to restore their access, arguing the ban violates the First Amendment. The decision to pull pooled TV coverage is a rare display of unified pushback from fiercely competitive networks against the administration's attempt to dictate what the public sees and how.…

item.description:
Candor and clarity of purpose are not themes traditionally associated with United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) meetings in New York. The annual summit, now in its 81st year, has long been a preferred venue for dictators and kleptocrats to make jargon-laden national — or, quite often, personal — cases against the West, while ironically doing so from the Big Apple, the beating heart of American capitalism. In response, American presidents over the past two decades have pushed past these theatrics, using the summits as opportunities to build consensus or rally support for the American position on global affairs. Not so with President Trump. And that may be a good thing.
